Applied to ScienceWorld as a case study, the framework reveals that **death avoidance accounts for ~90% of routing signal** (78.9% of non-tie labels from death asymmetry [A]; DAF=90.41% at P=100 [A]; r=0.9698, p=8.12e-07 [A] across 11 task types / 245 episodes [A]; source: plan-012-full). The framework further diagnoses that routing is nearly unnecessary (oracle ≈ always-deterministic, 96.3% agreement [A]), turning the router negative result into a validated framework prediction rather than a limitation. The contribution is the reusable diagnostic methodology + the case study finding, not the router architecture itself.

## Core Claims (3 claims for long paper) — [D126 reordered: framework-first]

**C1 (Diagnostic framework: episode-level counterfactual analysis)**: Per-step oracle labeling degenerates in sparse-reward environments (97.4% tie rate on ScienceWorld). We propose episode-level counterfactual analysis — running complete episodes under pure-internal and pure-deterministic strategies — as a **reusable diagnostic framework** that overcomes this circularity and decomposes routing signal into interpretable components (death avoidance vs non-death performance). The framework produces three diagnostic outputs: (1) penalty-independent label fraction (what % of routing decisions stem from catastrophic failure?), (2) Death Avoidance Factor decomposition (how much of the performance gap is death-driven?), (3) oracle degeneracy detection (is routing necessary at all?). Router training on framework-produced labels yields an **informative negative**: episode-level independent eval 47.1±2.2% < majority-vote 50.0% (8-seed cross-split, D089), and data scaling (25%–800%) shows no improvement — consistent with the framework's diagnosis that signal is task-type-level, not step-level learnable.

**C2 (Case study finding: death avoidance dominates ScienceWorld routing)**: Applied to ScienceWorld (11 task types, 245 episodes [A]), the framework reveals that **death avoidance is the dominant routing mechanism**: 78.9% of non-tie labels from death asymmetry [A], DAF=90.41% at P=100 [A] (Δ_full=+29.60, Δ_nd=+2.84 [A]), r=0.9698 (p=8.12e-07) [A]. Death rates: internal 42.9% / deterministic 16.3% [A]. Episode-level label distribution: det-preferred 86 / internal-preferred 9 / no-preference 150 [A]. Key exception: find-non-living-thing (n=40, zero deaths, Δ_full=+9.58, all non-death) [A]. The framework further diagnoses oracle degeneracy: 96.3% of oracle decisions match always-deterministic [A], meaning routing is nearly unnecessary — a framework prediction validated by the router negative result (C1). Death dominance resists four axes of intervention: retry (48→43.5%), Reflexion (48→34%, DAF>100% at N≥3), 10× scaling to 72B (DAF=92.4%), and prompt warning (48→37%).

**C3 (Cross-validation: model families + environment boundary probes)**: 
- **Cross-model**: Llama-3.1-8B full replication (N=220, 11 tasks): internal DR 41.4%, det DR 11.4%, ΔDR=+30.0pp, DAF=88.2%, direction consistency 10/10. Internal vulnerability ~42% is model-independent; det safety is model-dependent (16.3% vs 11.4%). Qwen-72B (N=255): DAF=92.4%, death dominance persists across capability levels.
- **Cross-domain boundary probes**: MATH (N=795, code interpreter): no catastrophic failure → no routing signal (+0.5pp, McNemar p=0.81). ALFWorld (135 games): 94.6% of non-tie labels favor information-advantaged strategy — qualitatively different mechanism (information asymmetry, not death avoidance), diagnosed by framework without modification.

Keyword heuristic structurally fails (D014) — further evidence that the signal the framework detects is not capturable by simple heuristics.

**Critical gap identified by all 3 Dream tiers**: The core pipeline (counterfactual labels → SFT small classifier → selective invocation) is standard in tool-use learning. Must position against:
- **Toolformer** (Schick et al. 2024): Self-supervised tool-use learning via API call insertion. SimGate differs: hindsight labels from environment forking (not self-supervised), safety-aware framing (not general tool selection).
- **ART** (Paranjape et al. 2023): Automated tool selection via LLM reasoning. SimGate: dedicated lightweight router, not LLM-as-router.
- **Chameleon** (Lu et al. 2024): LLM-as-planner routing to diverse tools. SimGate: single modality (deterministic computation), explicit small router.
- **ToolkenGPT** (Hao et al. 2024): Token-level tool triggers. SimGate: step-level routing with counterfactual labels.

**Our differentiation** [D126 framework-centric]: (1) **Diagnostic framework**, not tool selector — we provide a reusable methodology for decomposing routing signal, not a better router. (2) Episode-level counterfactual labeling overcomes per-step oracle circularity (97.4% tie rate). (3) Framework produces interpretable diagnostics: label fraction, DAF decomposition, oracle degeneracy detection. (4) Router negative result is a **validated framework prediction** (oracle degeneracy → routing unnecessary → router should fail), not a limitation. (5) Cross-domain boundary probes (MATH, ALFWorld) demonstrate framework generalizability.

Per-step oracle labeling degenerates in sparse-reward settings (97.4% tie rate on ScienceWorld). Tool-use methods (Toolformer, ART, Chameleon) learn general tool selection but don't decompose WHY tool invocation helps. The field lacks a diagnostic methodology for understanding routing signal composition.

- **Our contribution**: We develop episode-level counterfactual analysis as a diagnostic framework. By comparing complete episode outcomes under pure-internal and pure-deterministic strategies, the framework decomposes routing signal into interpretable components and detects oracle degeneracy. **ScienceWorld case study**: the framework reveals death avoidance accounts for ~90% of routing signal [A] (78.9% of non-tie labels from death asymmetry), and diagnoses that routing is nearly unnecessary (96.3% oracle-det agreement). Cross-domain probes (MATH: no death → no signal; ALFWorld: information asymmetry, not death) demonstrate framework applicability beyond the primary case study. Router training yields an informative negative (47.1% < majority-vote 50.0%) — a framework prediction, not a limitation.

- **Headline result template**: "We develop episode-level counterfactual analysis as a diagnostic framework for understanding when and why deterministic computation helps LLM agents. On ScienceWorld (11 task types, 245 episodes), the framework reveals that death avoidance accounts for 78.9% of routing labels and 90.4% of the performance gap (DAF; r=0.97, p<10⁻⁶), a finding that replicates across model families (Llama-8B, Qwen-72B) and resists four standard agent improvements. 1. **"Novelty is incremental — just SFT a small model to classify"**
   - Mitigation [D126 framework-centric]: Contribution is the **diagnostic framework** (episode-level counterfactual analysis), not the router. 2. **"Only one benchmark (ScienceWorld)"**
   - Mitigation [UPGRADED for long paper]: Multi-model validation (§4.2) shows finding holds across model families. MATH 795-problem evaluation (§4.3) demonstrates cross-domain applicability (code interpreter as deterministic oracle). ALFWorld exploratory evidence in Discussion.

3. **"Comparison unfair — CogRouter uses RL (CoPO), you use SFT"**
   - Mitigation: Our primary comparison is SimGate vs ablated baselines (always-internal, always-deterministic, random, heuristic) — all same training budget. CogRouter/ITP-R cited from papers for context.

4. **"Death avoidance is trivial — just always use deterministic"**
   - Mitigation: We do NOT claim selective > unconditional deterministic. Our contribution is the empirical finding that death avoidance dominates routing signal (~90% [A]), and the methodology that reveals this. Always-deterministic is a strong baseline — the interesting question is WHY (death avoidance), not WHETHER to route selectively. Plan-011 rule-based comparison + plan-012 death decomposition quantify this.

5. **"DAgger gap — SFT on pure-strategy trajectories may not transfer to mixed-strategy deployment"**
   - Mitigation: Acknowledge explicitly (cite Ross et al. 2011). Plan C exacerbates this: router trains on always-internal/always-deterministic trajectories but deploys on mixed. Note: Plan C's episode-level labels avoid oracle circularity (no per-step tie-breaking), which is a methodological advantage even if distribution shift remains.

\section{Introduction}

Large language models deployed as interactive agents must repeatedly decide \emph{how} to compute: reason internally, or delegate to an external tool.
In ScienceWorld \cite{scienceworld-2022}, a text-based science simulation, internal reasoning is error-prone---the model may hallucinate state changes (e.g., that water has boiled when the stove was never activated)---while deterministic external computation eliminates such errors via exact state transitions. The practical question: \emph{when should an agent route computation externally versus internally?}

Existing routing approaches frame this as a capability or efficiency decision: Toolformer \cite{toolformer-2023} inserts API calls by perplexity reduction; ART \cite{art-2023} decomposes tasks into tool-augmented programs; Chameleon \cite{chameleon-2023} selects heterogeneous modules per subtask; adaptive-computation methods route to different reasoning depths \cite{cogrouter-2026,ares-2026} or model tiers \cite{mtrouter-2026}; concurrent analyses further presuppose diverse routing signals~\citep{when2tool-2026,tool-use-tax-2026,to-call-or-not-2026}. The shared assumption---that routing signal stems from diverse sources and a learned router can exploit it---has not been tested: no prior work has decomposed what drives routing decisions in interactive environments.

We propose a \emph{diagnostic framework} comprising (i)~episode-level counterfactual labeling under pure strategies (\S\ref{sec:collection}--\ref{sec:labeling}), and (ii)~the Death Avoidance Factor (DAF), which decomposes the routing score gap into death-avoidance and non-death components (\S\ref{sec:daf}). Applied to ScienceWorld, \textbf{78.9\% of non-tie routing labels arise from death asymmetry} (75 of 95), a penalty-independent finding. 3	\paragraph{Tool Use and External Computation in LLMs.}
